utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I stop you, Mr. Sejmenovic. I'm going to come on to the steps you took later. I just want to go back for a moment to first something you just said and then this document, to complete it. You told us that you were aware of artillery placements around the area. By the time of this meeting, could you see the artillery surrounding the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The artillery had surrounded Kozarac even before this meeting took place. At some locations, the artillery had been placed long time before, immediately after the return of the 5th Kozarac Brigade in the battlefield in Croatia, for instance, at Urije, located at the outskirts of Prijedor. The artillery had been there for a very long time, and it was not --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that yesterday. What I want to know is had there been any further movement of artillery in the area of --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the takeover and before the period I'm talking about, sometime in mid-May, there was further movement of artillery, for instance, in the area above Kozarac, near the quarry. One of such locations was Benkovac, as well. Mortars were positioned near the road, below the road, 1 kilometre away from Kozarac. There were mortars positioned from the direction of Omarska, from the vicinity of the village of Hadzici, a Bosniak village. Artillery was also positioned at the Tomasica hill with the barrels turned towards Kozarac. This artillery was also positioned during the period of time I'm talking about. This was observed -- most of this was observed by local farmers. And there was no resistance whatsoever to this type of activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can we just come back briefly to this document. You've told us you first heard about this order to disarm at this meeting. Were any announcements made over the radio, that you heard, saying that weapons must be surrendered?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an announcement to that effect at the time of this meeting, but its broadcast intensified after the meeting. It could be heard every hour over the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This talks about illegally acquired weapons. First of all, did people, in fact, surrender their weapons as a result of this ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the ultimatum, and prior to the ultimatum for a brief period, all weapons owned by people in Kozarac was within the TO. Regardless of the quality of these weapons. Handmade rifles, old Turkish Kubara guns, pistols from Second World War, handmade pistols, hunting rifles, weapons belonging to the police and to the TO, as well as weapons that had been purchased privately, mostly by Serbs in Omarska. All these weapons were listed and given to the Kozarac TO. The Serbian Crisis Staff treated all these weapons as illegal weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that include, therefore, weapons for which people had permits, legally issued permits?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Just to give you an example, hunting rifles, pistols, weapons with authorisation, people owned authorisations for these weapons, and they obtained those authorisation certificates long before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this ultimatum for illegally acquired weapons apply to Serbs as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I want to move then just quickly to two other aspects that are dealt with in these conclusions. First, it states in Item 4 that war plans had to be analysed and approved by the council for national defence, or the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region. "Only persons who are absolutely loyal to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina can be placed in management positions in enterprises." Now, before the takeover on the 30th of April, 1992, were management positions held by persons of non-Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was an equal distribution of Serbs and non-Serbs in the managerial positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the takeover, what was the situation in respect of non-Serbs who held management positions in enterprises?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people were dismissed and replaced by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, it states that "all persons who fail to respond to the above calls shall be forbidden," that is, to return to the municipality, "shall be forbidden to return to their homes in the territory of the ARK and all their movable and immovable property shall be confiscated." How was that put into effect?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was put into effect soon after the attack on parts of Prijedor, Hambarine, and Kozarac. They began to confiscate private property. They started with the most valuable items, and then forbade people to return to their homes, those houses at least that had not been destroyed. And then very soon we noticed other people moving into these houses. During the first days, when they confiscated someone's car, they would issue the person with a certificate to the effect that this was only temporary confiscation. But later on, property was confiscated and no further certificates were issued. They started to loot, confiscate, and rob in an organised way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come on to that later. This decision doesn't specify any ethnicity. It says: "All male persons fit for war". Were there any Serbs, to your knowledge, who had left the area and had their property confiscated?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of a single case like that. There may have been such cases, but at least not in the area where I lived and where I was familiar with the situation. And there were a number of Serbian households there. Some people had been absent from the area for a while, but their property was not confiscated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Sejmenovic. That's what I want to ask you about this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd move for its full admission, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Here, I can't ask the Defence because the Bench has doubts, and the time is not yet right for a decision. Probably the underlying document was another one because apparently when you only look on the numbers, the one in Cyrillic ends with 6, and English was 5. Probably it's a typo or numerous typos only. When you see the scope of underlining, it's different. And then it would be of major interest, apparently on the B/C/S document, there seems to be an additional headline indicating that it was sent by fax. Therefore, it's indispensable to have the original before us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before I deal with the steps that you took I want to return for a moment to the political scene that was happening. Did you become aware of a meeting in Banja Luka on the 12th of May of the Serbian assembly, the Serbian Republic assembly?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew at that time that there had been meetings of Serbian assemblies. Sometimes, we were able to watch TV or listen to the radio. I didn't know much about the specific issues discussed by these assemblies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall an announcement being made as to the goals of the Serbian -- the Bosnian Serb Republic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The goals were proclaimed publicly in different programmes. Announcements by Crisis Staffs were usually followed by announcements of the leaders at the local level and the regional level. At least as far as public announcements were concerned, everything was subordinated to the overriding plan of creating a Serb state. These were clear views. There was no more hide and seek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall the announcement that a declaration of the Serbian Republic and its own army within Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I'd like you, please, to have a look at the document with the 65 ter number 147, which are the minutes of the meeting held on the 12th of May in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the same position before, that I'm going to ask him about the knowledge of the persons involved and the things said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Provisional number will be, then, S141. But let's please proceed in the same way as with the last minutes we had yesterday. Read out what is necessary those parts, and only those parts then will be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If I may at this point object. And the reason for my objection is that this is just an attempt to circumvent what this witness has just previously said on page 49, line 16 through 17 where the witness clearly states that he doesn't or did not know about the specific issues discussed by these assemblies. Now counsel is either trying to refresh his recollection or have this witness Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. attempt to read what we can argue at times is left best for our own interpretation or the interpretation by witnesses who were present, or experts who have reviewed these documents and give their opinions on that. This witness was clearly not at the assembly meeting on May 12th, 1992; he clearly states he did not see it on television or hear about it on the radio. And clearly and unequivocally acknowledged that he did not know any of the specific issues that were discussed at this assembly. So I object on those grounds and think that it would be highly improper to let this witness now to review this document and give us any testimony in connection with that based upon what he previously just told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we went through this same argument with the minutes of the 11th of December. It is clear, because I've referred to some of the issues that are discussed during this meeting, that the witness did, in fact, hear about some of the issues. He knows many of the people who are involved in these discussions, and he is able to assist to that extent. And it may well be once his memory is refreshed from it, he's able to say that he did see some of this on television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Indeed. It it's restricted to facts known by the witness only, and if the document and only the parts of the document will serve for as Defence counsel said correctly "refresh the memory of the witness," then it may do so. Therefore, objection rejected.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This, as I've said, Mr. Sejmenovic, was held -- this assembly was held on the 12th of May, 1992, in Banja Luka, chaired by the president of the assembly, Mr. Krajisnik. And if we look at the agenda, it includes a report on the political conditions and the war, as it's described, in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And it then deals with various other matters that are to be considered. Adopting text of the oath, confirmation of the decisions and other legislation, and then amendments to the constitution and so on and so forth. However, if we turn, please, to the next page in our translation, we see the proposed text of the oath. "I swear I shall abide by the constitution and the laws of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I shall protect its constitutional system honourably and faithfully, respecting moral standards and spiritual values and the struggle for the freedom of Serbian people and all other citizens of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so help me God." I'm stopping there, Mr. Sejmenovic. Did you come to hear what the exact terms of the oath that had to be taken was?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May we also, Your Honour, have a time reference as to when the witness learned of this oath, whether it was yesterday during the proofing or whether it was ten years ago just to keep the question clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, I accept that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you heard first of all, and then secondly, when you heard.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this form of the oath, or the specific oath where the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is referred to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The oath, the text which was apparently adopted, which you can read under Item 2.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear this oath, but I can't tell you the exact period. Was it May, was it June of 1992, or later? I really can't say, I'm afraid. I can't remember. But I did hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was obliged to take this oath to the Serbian Republic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ministers, government members, deputies to the parliament were obliged to take this oath. And there was an identical oath that was used when the Serbian Municipal Assemblies were being set up, except that instead of the name of the Republic, the name of the municipality was used. This oath, for example, was spoken in Prijedor in early 1992 in the theatre when the Serbs organised the establishment of the Serbian municipality, a very similar oath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you move, please, to page -- it's page 7 of the translation. And you will see there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, just for clarification. We should be aware that we are discussing a different document now. We started with the minutes. And then on page 4, the minutes are ending. And then we have to go into another document which in English I can identify as original minutes. There should be a clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour is quite right because we move from the agenda session minutes to original minutes which are a separate document. Your Honour is quite right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can go to page 7 of the translation, which is in the second part of these minutes. And Mr. Sejmenovic, could you find, please, the speech or an intervention after Mr. Krajisnik has opened the session, we see that a man called Radislav Vukic speaks.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, do you know who Mr. Vukic was?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the president of the Banja Luka branch of the SDS as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he makes a proposal that after the first item has been completed, "we will move on to discussion of the bill on the armed forces and draft decision on establishing the armed forces staff while we are still rested and fresh, and while the commanders are still here." Now, I want to ask you this: Do you recall seeing on television a session of the assembly at which senior leaders of the military were present; that is to say, Mladic and Talic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see this on TV later on. At that time, we couldn't watch TV. But later on, it was quite regular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember -- when you say "later on," how much later was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see, so these were things you saw after you left. Can we then move, please, to the next speech of Mr. Karadzic. And he suggests -- he said, close to the beginning of the speech: "In Bosnia and Herzegovina over the last two years since the founding of the HDZ, first in Croatia and then in Herzegovina, and later in Bosnia too, with its militant and dangerous gatherings with the insignia of the Ustasha regime who has committed genocide against us and the setting up of the SDA at it founding assembly with their militant Islamic fundamentalism." Now, had you heard Mr. Karadzic described the HDZ and the SDA in those terms before this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are speaking about Mr. Karadzic's speeches in the Bosnia and Herzegovina parliament he did not use such extreme expressions. But if we're talking about party meetings and the SDS party policies, yes, they were labelled in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you actually, when you say he was in the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina, he didn't use such extreme expressions. Had you actually seen him or heard him using those expressions on television or in the press?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Later on it became standard fare, the vocabulary he was using.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, still -- and I'm afraid it's quite difficult to find. This is still Mr. Karadzic's speech. It's at the bottom of the translation, page 11, and it's -- the sentence begins "Such a solution" -- I'm sorry, I should take it back. "We found a solution with the United Nations for Serbian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the beginning of a passage or is it --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. My fault. The passage begins: "We understand the pressure from the OSCE to which we belong."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right, I just found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Right at the bottom, or very close to the end of the bottom, there's a sentence that begins: "We tried to reconcile our internal situation and our interests with the interests of others."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The part I want to ask you about is this: "Such a solution was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not on the horizon in Bosnia and Herzegovina" -- I'm sorry. I ought to read the whole passage so we can put it into context. "We tried to reconcile our internal situation and our interests with the interests of others outside of us. Those who live outside of us, and that is how we found a solution with the United Nations for Serbian Krajina which, as a sort of respite, may allow us to describe the position of our Serbian brothers in Krajina and their preparation for unification and joining a common state, that is, an alliance of states or a Serbian Federation. Such a solution was not on the horizon in Bosnia and Herzegovina, nor could it be implemented in the way it was in Croatia because huge forces would be needed to cover the Serbian territory in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Besides, we ask why Serbian territory has to be covered. Why not cover Muslim territory, which is much smaller and much more problematic in the state and legal sense, because the laws are not being respected, and terror is being used there." Now, the suggestion being made in that speech or that part of the speech, I should say, is that the Muslim parts of the territory in Bosnia and Herzegovina, laws were not being respected, and terror was being used there. Do you know to what Dr. Karadzic was referring by this reference?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably meant that the laws of the Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina were not being observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about "terror is being used there"?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with any outbreaks of terror in these areas, at least as far as the area in which I lived is concerned. On the contrary, the Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina and its institutions exercised terror over the remaining population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then can we look now at the goals that Dr. Karadzic set out for the Bosnian Serbs and which you say you knew about. If we go, please, to page 13 of the translation, and if you can find, Mr. Sejmenovic, the passage that begins "the Serbian side in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the presidency, the government, the council for national security..." et cetera. And it may be Mr. Lukic can assist if he has the page number in the Bosnian version, Cyrillic version. Have you found the passage?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it after these -- is it on the previous page with respect to the portion we just read?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, it's further on from that. If you go to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's at the bottom of page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've just found it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. The paragraph begins or the passage begins: "The Serbian side in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the presidency, the government, the council for national security which we have set up have formulated strategic priorities; that is to say, the strategic goals for the Serbian people. The first such goal is separation from the other two national communities, separation of states, separation from those who are our enemies and who have used every opportunity, especially in this century, to attack us, and who would continue with such practices if we were to continue to stay together in the same state." Mr. Sejmenovic, had you heard that goal expressed before May, or was this the first time when you heard about it afterwards, after this meeting of the 12th of May?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard about it before. It had been publicly discussed before the first negotiations took place at the level of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Karadzic publicly demanded the so-called ethnic division and suggested that Serbs should be separated from the rest of the population. If Muslims or Bosniaks and Croats wanted to go their own way, they could remain together. But as far as Serbs were concerned, his position was that Serbs should be physically separated from others, both along ethnic lines and in terms of public institutions. He said that they would establish and create Serbian banks, Serbian PTT, Serb streets. However, what was problematic was the fact that he considered some of the areas which were actually non-Serb to be part of the Serb territories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had he before -- I'm sorry, I should have made the question a bit clearer. Had he before said that effectively, he wanted the separation because non-Serbs were enemies and have used every opportunity to attack and would continue attacking?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He had never expressed himself in that way publicly before, by referring to others as enemies and as potential attackers against Serbs. No. Such terms had never been used by him prior to the establishment of the Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we deal with the second strategic goal. "It seems to me is a corridor between Semberija and Krajina. That is something which we may be forced to sacrifice something here and there. But it is of the utmost strategic importance for the Serbian people because it integrates the Serbian lands not only of Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina, but integrates Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina with Serbian Krajina and Serbian Krajina with the Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia. So that is a strategic goal that has been placed high on the priority list that we have to achieve because Bosnian Krajina, Serbian Krajina or the alliance of states or Serbian Federation is not feasible if we fail to secure that corridor which will integrate us, which will provide us with unimpeded flow from one part of our state to another." Did you hear about this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. Just for our clarification, good to know that the Bench in part can follow the Cyrillic lines. We were surprised by reading Semberija in English. Could the witness please turn to page 8, second paragraph, the three last words. Have you ever seen these words before, and what is special with this Semberija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Semberija is a part of Bosnia and Herzegovina bordering on Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification in this context. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this corridor that had to be created, had you heard reference to this before May?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not before May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about it either at the time or after this meeting of the 12th of May?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it after the meeting of the 12th of May, shortly after that. The word "corridor" was the most frequently mentioned word over the radio because parts of the 5th Kozara Brigade had been sent to the front line to establish and defend this corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this goal, as it was expressed, to set up a corridor between Semberija and the Krajina, did that have any direct effect on the Prijedor municipality? Did its positioning have any importance for this idea of a corridor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wouldn't have any importance if Bosnia and Herzegovina existed. It could only have significance in case these Serb territories are separated and needed to be connected with Serbia. Because several areas are relevant here, if you look at the map. Some of these areas do not have natural, physical connection with Serbia, and the corridor was needed in order to establish this communication in order to link up these Serb areas with the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to this need to link up the Serb areas, where did Prijedor fit in it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prijedor is located far away from the corridor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can we deal very quickly, then, with the last goals. The third strategic goal was to establish another corridor in the Drina valley. And the fourth strategic goal, the establishment on the border on the Una and Neretva Rivers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It think it may as well be if, after the break, we just look at a very quick map, or a map quickly, rather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the fifth strategic goal is the division of the city of Sarajevo into Serbian and Muslim parts, and the sixth strategic goal is the access of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the sea. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's a little bit early, but it's a good place to stop. We would like to look at that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The trial stands adjourned until 2.00 sharp. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.27 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And once again, we have before us a question to deal with the next three months. The six strategic goals, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What I was about to do, Your Honour, was we've blown up part of a full map of Bosnia and Herzegovina which has not yet been exhibited, but it's the easiest way to show this. And the Defence have seen a copy and don't object, I understand. I wonder -- the best thing is for it to be put on the ELMO, and Your Honour, we'll provide copies for the Chamber and to the Defence by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I appreciate, registry, that it will be 142? Wasn't the previous one -- okay, fine. 142 provisionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's identify first of all, please, Mr. Sejmenovic, for the -- it's not really that clear, but can we just identify Prijedor. We can move the map slightly towards the right.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prijedor is here where I'm showing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate, and I think we'll have to map to its very edge where Semberija is. Yes, we'll have to push the map along. Can we move the map.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the area of Semberija. And here across the border is the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we can see one of the major towns there is Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Bijeljina is the administrative centre, not only administrative, but also the economic and political centre of the Semberija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you, if you were travelling through this area, in other words from Serbia through Semberija, and you wanted to go as is said in the second strategic goal the Krajina, the Autonomous Region of Krajina, what would the route -- the most simple route be? For example, let's take a purely hypothetical example, you want troops to come from Serbia through this -- to go towards the Krajina, and then Croatia, what would be the most straightforward route or the best route?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The best or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm hesitant that the witness could answer such a question, to be honest. The first portion of your question was more adequate, which would be the normal travel route. I have not the impression that our witness is an expert on defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should ask, first of all, have you ever travelled, Mr. Sejmenovic --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most usual --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't catch the answer there.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most usual route to take, if one was to travel from this area here to the parts of Croatia that you mentioned, would be via Vinkovci, because the roads are much better over there. However, there is an alternative route across Tuzla, Doboj, Banja Luka, Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, and then further on to Croatia. If one wanted to travel to Serb ethnic territories --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop for a moment. Just so that we can see it, because the maps -- you would say you would go from Bijeljina to Tuzla. Can we move the map so we can see Doboj. And then you said to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to Banja Luka. Or Bijeljina, Brcko, Derventa, Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you wanted to go into the Croatian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you wanted to go to the Croatian Krajina from Banja Luka, you would have to go to Prijedor, then to Bosanski Novi, and then further on to Croatia; or Bosanski Novi, Bosanska Krupa, Bihac, and then Croatia depending on your destination in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But either route would take you through Prijedor, whether you went through Krupa or Novi?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have arrived at Banja Luka from that direction, then you would have to continue to Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, Bosanska Krupa, and Bihac. Of course, you would have to pass through Prijedor. Prijedor can be bypassed only if you go to Novo Gradiska, which is a different destination in Croatia. If you wanted to go to the Croatian Krajina, then the best way would be Prijedor, Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can we just, while you've still got the map, deal with this: The fourth strategic goal was the establishment of the border on the Una and Neretva Rivers. Can you just indicate the Una River, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The River Una can be seen here on the map, depicted in blue, running from Bosanski Novi to Bihac and further on. I am now following the Una River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can one see on the map -- it may not be on it -- the Neretva River? Maybe not.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Neretva River cannot be seen on this portion of the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just roughly tell us where that is.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is here, in this area compared to the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just bring the map down slightly. So it's below Sarajevo, is it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Unless there are any other areas that Your Honours would like the witness to point out, that's all that I intend to ask.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Unless there are any other areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Not at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. You can take the map away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, one more question. Hand the map back. It says the sixth strategic goal is the access of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the sea. Where was the nearest access to the sea that Bosnia and Herzegovina would have?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you zoom in, please. Can this portion here be enlarged, please? The other way around. Can we see all of this part on the ELMO, please. The shortest way to the coast from Bosnia and Herzegovina was here, if we had the remainder of the map, we would be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think we get the general idea. I'm just seeing if I can see what the nearest big town is. We can see, I think, it's not very clear, but is this right, we can see Knin on the left of the map?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can Knin here, but Bosnia and Herzegovina have access to the coast in the area of Neum, where I'm indicating with the pointer. And that is the closest way to the coast. Neum is the direct access to the coast, but there's also an area which is very close to the border of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sejmenovic. Now you really can take the map away. Now, I want to move, leaving Mr. Karadzic's speech, to a couple of other speeches that were made during that session. And I just want to find -- yes -- it's a speech made by a man called Kalinic. It's on page 22 of the translation. And for your purposes, Mr. Sejmenovic, if you go through -- carry on in the record, after Karadzic, you get somebody called Beli, and then somebody called Mr. Milosevic, who is not I hasten to add the Milosevic who is on trial. Then Mr. Radic, Trifko Radic, Mr. Djuric, and then finally Mr. Kalinic.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found this passage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, first of all, had you ever heard or met somebody called Dragan Kalinic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Dragan Kalinic from the assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He was a member of the opposition. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was still a member of the assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, what were his views like? Were they moderate, extreme?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His views were rather moderate. He was not a member of the SDS, but a member of one of the left-wing parties and was a member of this very active opposition in the assembly, together with other deputies of mixed ethnic origin. He was very often opposed to the intentions and positions of the SDS. I'm referring to his actual speeches and interventions at the parliament. I remember when the declaration on independence was discussed, that he was against it. And he spoke publicly against it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's -- I'm sorry. And the other thing is, was there as far, as you could see from the time that you were in the assembly, and both he and Brdjanin were there, was there any special relation? I'm sorry. Did they seem particularly close or friendly or express similar views?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to judge by their statements and discussions in which they took part at the parliament, they did not seem close at all. And before these discussions, they were never seen together or in any kind of contact, Kalinic and members of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can we just have a look for a moment at what -- part of what Mr. Kalinic had to say at this session. As you say rightly, he -- it doesn't seem he was a member of the party because he says: "Gentlemen and ladies, I will speak on behalf of the group of independent deputies of this assembly. I would like first to apologise for appearing on this stand in such inappropriate attire. It is because we are at war, and we all brought what we could." And he then says: "I would like to address some of the things I have heard here and some of the information and ideas that have been in circulation lately, which would create a certain confusion among our people, and maybe this would be the right place to clear such issues up while there is still time. Among all the issues, this assembly should decide on, the most important one is this: Have we chosen the option of war or the option of negotiation? I say this with a reason, and I must instantly add that knowing who our enemies are, how perfidious they are, how they cannot be trusted until they are physically, militarily destroyed, and crushed, which, of course, implies eliminating and liquidating their key people. I do not hesitate in selecting the first option, the option of war because I believe that our fate, the fate of Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I do not link it in any way to the fate of Serbia and Montenegro. I have said this before, our sentimental and national bonds in this respect must be reduced in this respect to a pragmatic level and established on the basis of interest, that the fate of Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina cannot be solved in any other way but by war. It is possible that in doing this, the fate of our Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina would be to chose a hundred years of solitude over 500 years of slavery under some new Turkish empire. We will find ourselves in an extreme isolation, and will only have ourselves to rely on. We have to calculate on this, and I will be the first one to say here that I am ready, as probably most of you are, to share this fate with our people. "Why do I say that the option of war seems more likely to me? Because only what has been conquered militarily may become really and truly ours." I'm going to come back and ask you something about this in a moment, but I'd like you just to go on, please, for a moment to find Mr. Brdjanin's speech, which is on our page 29. And for your purposes, Mr. Sejmenovic, it comes -- there are three speeches in between. One by Mr. Kupresanin, and then Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found the speech of Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Radislav Brdjanin: "Mr. President, I asked for the floor only after I realised that I was the most remote, that compared to everything else, I am the kindergarten. I would like first of all -- I would first of all like to thank all those participating in the discussion. I would like to say a heartfelt bravo to Mr. Kalinic in all my appearances in this joint assembly, it has never crossed my mind that although he seems quiet, while I seem hawkish, his opinions are the closest to mine. I believe that this is the formula and that we should adhere to this formula." In other words, at that stage, Mr. Sejmenovic, it appears that Mr. Brdjanin is echoing what you have described about Mr. Kalinic in being quiet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Defence tries to take the floor a couple minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pardon me. Your Honour, at this point we object to this line of questioning as it relates to Mr. Kalinic, and also I truly believe, although I know we've modified the rule somewhat, and not so far as reading the entire text of the speech and incorporating with what the witness earlier testified about, this witness's more moderate views, but how does that in any way relate or how does it connect up with Dr. Stakic who was never alleged to have been at this meeting or have any relationship with Brdjanin or Mr. Kalinic. In this case, I think what we're trying to do, unfortunately, is to cloud the issues that are before us, and if you read on and read the entire text of not just this document, but other issues, Mr. Kalinic is specifically referring to the war that's occurring in Sarajevo, and that's the war that they are debating. He also talks about various Green Berets that I don't want to again poison the entire record by suggesting that there were or there were not. We could address that later in my cross-examination. He also testifies about certain mercenaries coming from various different countries and he cites a specific number. It really doesn't have anything to do, and he goes on to discuss Sarajevo in quite some detail and the war. How does that have anything to do with Prijedor? As we saw on the map it's remotely distant. And I would object on the grounds that it's irrelevant and also there's leading questions by the OTP in connection with what Brdjanin thought and whether those were his thoughts. If this witness can tell us what Brdjanin thought about Mr. Kalinic, I would agree that he can testify to that only after we establish the foundation that such testimony is relevant, which I still have not unfortunately been able to determine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour. That's the difficulty. I'm sorry about this, but the documents that you see listed, a lot of them deal with this aspect of the case. utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we are all aware of this, and we are aware of this idea of the OTP having this overall view what they regard has happened in former Yugoslavia and the link between all incidents, accidents, serious crimes committed there. utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, it's the intervening link that's important. utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sejmenovic, I want to move what you began to talk about before the break, and that was actions you took in respect of the TO in Kozarac after that meeting that you had with the SDS in around mid-May. Can you tell us what actions were taken?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was decided to complete the organisation of the TO as soon as possible, and to have the TO defend the territory, to make this its function. As the organisation of the TO could not be carried out as ordered by the territorial staff, the only thing we could do is do it at the local level, meaning at the Kozarac local commune level and other local communes belonging to the same area. At the local level, the people in charge of these tasks intensified their activity, and they tried to organise as quickly as possible the TO units and charged them with protecting the Kozarac area. Following the meeting at which we had been given the ultimatum, a meeting of the citizens, as we used to refer to it, was convened. A mass rally attended by all prominent persons, as well as all those who came there to see what the result of the meeting was. It was also attended by all local leaders. The discussion at the meeting with the SDS was conveyed in full, the result of our discussions with Arsic and Zeljaja, and then some people came forward with their opinions on what they thought was best in terms of what we should do next. And they were seeking any possibility to re-establish contact with the SDS. They elaborated theories on the future course of events and the possibilities that were involved. Everyone's conclusion, based on the overall situation, as well as on the results of the meeting that had been held was that the army was ready to attack Kozarac. Regardless of that, we decided to keep trying to re-establish our contact with the SDS and to ask the SDS, Colonel Arsic and Zeljaja, to have talks again, to resume negotiations. And at the same time, endeavours were made to organise, in the best possible way, the TO members and the weapons available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you pause there for a moment. Let's just deal with these two possibilities. First of all, were you able to re-establish contact with either Colonel Arsic or Major Zeljaja before the attack happened?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that attempts were made on a daily basis, and I know that it was all to no avail. I know that at a certain point, those from Prijedor accepted to talk, perhaps one day before the attack took place or just at the beginning of the attack. I know that some people did go to have talks, and I know that these people who had gone never returned. Our suspicion was that they had been killed, but then they were registered at missing persons for years after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened then about the organisation in the best possible way, as you put it, of TO members? What was actually done?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean before the attack?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What did you, in Kozarac, in the Kozarac region, try and do?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried to have all the weapons available no matter if those were TO weapons, police weapons, handmade weapons or illegally purchased weapons. We tried to organise all of this through the TO. Formally speaking, the TO could always be extended, if necessary. So we began this process. It was completed, in part, at least as far as the administrative part was concerned, before the attack. But the deployment of units was never completed before the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in order to establish -- now, I'm sorry, I'll go back one rung from there. Were lists kept, first of all, of people who were members of the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the weaponry that the TO held? Were there lists available of that, or did lists have to be compiled at the time, that is, between the 15th of May and the end of May?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must provide an additional explanation concerning the function of the TO before the war. In each of the local communes, the TO was pursuant to past laws, it had a limited, usually very small, number of members. You knew exactly who the members were and who would sign for the weapons if necessary. After the general mobilisation was proclaimed by the Autonomous Region of Krajina, we were facing a situation where our TO had to be enlarged. We did not have any records, and I know that people went searching through the local communes, the lists of voters, records of the census. We tried to have these records updated to suit the needs of the TO. The local authorities made another very important decision. Regardless of the legal right of the TO to mobilise people regardless of their will, we made a decision to enlarge the TO on a voluntary basis only. We said that each and every one of the citizens should be visited in person, regardless of their nationality, those who had remained in this isolated area, and that they should then agree or disagree to become members of the TO. And in case the person agreed, they should sign the document to the effect. And as far as these persons had any weapons, the weapons, too, should be recorded beside the name. Those who did not want to join or were not able to join simply didn't sign. And later on, they were not regarded as members of this enlarged TO body. Some of the activities that I'm talking about were completed in the month of May before the attack, which means that records had been drawn up for the needs of the TO. Some of them were shown to a number of individuals who then signed them. We recorded the existing weapons and the persons who owned these weapons, and we started to assign those who had agreed to join to certain units. But this was only the beginning, and there was no time to complete this process. So a number of units only existed on paper, and they never really existed in practice because there wasn't enough time to set them up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm now going to show the witness a couple of documents in relation to this. So that may be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then this map is admitted into evidence as S142. And the trial stands adjourned until 3.25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we see over the beginning part which says: "Territorial Defence staff Kozarac," there appears to be a stamp of some kind across those words.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The stamp reads: "Territorial Defence, Bosnia and Herzegovina; Territorial Defence staff, Kozarac."

utterances.text: Was that an official stamp?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go to the last page of the document for a moment, please. And can we see there number 106, your name?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.text: Number 88.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also a pistol. Under 95 and 96, we read the names of Dzemal Hodzic and Dervis Hodzic, they did not sign the list which means that they did not make themselves available to the TO. utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was taking these lists round? Were people going to individuals homes armed with this list, or were people asked to go into the TO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
